meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Why does my son have a zero?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
Walk me through it, then. But I'll tell you what I'm not hearing yet, Hale: why a zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
I'm writing down 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM. Which night, Hale, and can I see that history myself?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and the version history, with its dates, sent to me in writing. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position. Nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the version history with dates in front of her.
What moved her: Giving exact times and word counts from the version history got her writing things down and asking a real question, but with no date and nothing she could read herself, it went no further.
What cost ground: Moving on without answering why the zero went in before anyone called her left the process complaint standing, and it is the strongest thing she has.
Try next time: Right after her first question, own in one sentence that the zero went in before the call home, then turn the screen and show the version history with its date.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
